newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel warns Syria against starting war.
newsitem.headline: Israel warns Syria against starting war.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai peered down at Syria on Wednesday from on top of the occupied Golan Heights and warned Damascus against launching any aggression.
"We hope the Syrian President (Hafez al-)Assad and the Syrian government and the Syrian people understand the situation and are not trying to damage the situation," Mordechai told reporters.
The Israeli defence minister visited Israeli army outposts on the Golan Heights which Israel captured from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war.
Syria wants Israel to withdraw fully from the strategic plateau in exchange for peace. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's hardline government rejects trading land for peace with the Arabs.
Syria's movement of thousands of troops in Lebanon last month from Beirut to the foot of the Golan Heights near the border with Israel caused war jitters in the Jewish state.
"I'm observing the Syrian area on the other side of the Golan Heights and I'm going to have some briefing about the...situation in this area," Mordechai said.
Sporadic peace talks between the two countries since 1991 have foundered over the fate of the Golan.
Mordechai repeated a proposal made also by Israel's previous centre-left government that Assad come to Jerusalem to talk peace despite the city being in hot dispute between Palestinians and Israel.
"I'm inviting President Assad to come to Jerusalem to discuss all the issues in dispute," Mordechai said.

Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem along with the rest of the West Bank in 1967. It annexed Jerusalem shortly thereafter. Palestinians want East Jerusalem to be the capital of a future independent state.
